procedural_matters: Frederik Jensen (competitor sail DEN 225625) attended the hearing as an observer.
CRO 219191 did not ask to withdraw the protest after the arbitration meeting and neither boat took a Post-Race Penalty under RRS T1(a).
facts: At themoment of the incident there were 14 knots of wind and choppy water.
The incidenthappened close to the Race Committee vessel, 20 seconds to the startingsignal of race #4.
The start of race #4 was under RRS 30.4.
CRO 219191 was layingon the starting line on starboard tack on a reaching course almost 90 degreesto the wind.
DEN 210987 was sailingon port three and half boat lengths behind the line.
DEN 210987 tacked andwhen the tack was completed she established an overlap to leeward withCRO 219191 at alateral distance of one and half boat length.
Contact occurred between the starboard side of the bow of DEN 210987 and the port bow side of CRO 219191.
The Race Committeeidentified CRO 219191 andDEN 210987 as being in the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and thefirst mark and scored both boats BFD.
The Race Committeedisplayed the General Recall and the sail numbers of CRO 219191 andDEN 210987 weredisplayed on a board before the next warning signal.
Neither of themsailed the next start.
There was nodamage to either boat.
conclusions: CRO 219191 towindward failed to keep clear of DEN 210987 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
Since the race wasrestarted after the General Recall, and since CRO 219191 had caused neitherinjury nor serious damage, she shall not be penalized further, RRS 36(b).
Since DEN 210987 was right-of-way boat and the contact did not cause damage or injury, she isexonerated under RRS 43.1(c) for breaking RRS 14.
CRO 219191’s score in race #4 was made significantly worse through her own fault. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b) are not met.
decision: Protest upheld. Since the provision of RRS 36(b) applies, no penalty is imposed on CRO 219191 under rule 60.5(c)(3).
